hello-polite.meaningNote: Standard polite greeting suitable for any time of day.

good-evening.meaningNote: Formal or polite greeting after sunset.
good-evening.exampleSentence: Good evening, we have a table reserved.

how-are-you.meaningNote: Casual and friendly check-in on someone's well-being.
how-are-you.exampleSentence: Hi Maria, how are you doing today?

nice-to-meet-you.meaningNote: Courteous phrase when introduced to someone for the first time.
nice-to-meet-you.exampleSentence: I am Carlos, nice to meet you.

thank-you-very-much.meaningNote: Expression of deep or sincere gratitude.
thank-you-very-much.exampleSentence: Thank you very much for your kind assistance.

you-are-welcome.exampleSentence: You are welcome, happy to help anytime.

please.meaningNote: Fundamental marker of politeness when requesting anything.
please.exampleSentence: Could you please pass the water?

excuse-me-pardon.meaningNote: Used to capture attention politely or to pass through a crowd.
excuse-me-pardon.exampleSentence: Excuse me, may I get past?

goodbye-take-care.meaningNote: Warm parting phrase wishing safety to the other person.
goodbye-take-care.exampleSentence: Goodbye, take care on your flight home!

a-table-for-two-please.meaningNote: Standard request when entering a restaurant.
a-table-for-two-please.exampleSentence: Good evening, a table for two inside, please.

can-i-see-the-menu.text: May I see the menu, please?
can-i-see-the-menu.meaningNote: Requesting the printed or digital food selection.
can-i-see-the-menu.exampleSentence: Excuse me, may I see the menu and drink specials?

what-do-you-recommend.meaningNote: Inquiring about house specialties or popular local delicacies.
what-do-you-recommend.exampleSentence: Everything looks tasty; what do you recommend here?

the-check-please.text: Could we have the check, please?
the-check-please.meaningNote: Signaling the server that you are ready to settle payment.
the-check-please.exampleSentence: We are all done, could we have the check, please?

i-am-allergic-to-peanuts.meaningNote: Vital health safety advisory for food preparers.
i-am-allergic-to-peanuts.exampleSentence: Please ensure there are no nuts in this; I am allergic to peanuts.

is-this-dish-spicy.meaningNote: Clarifying the chili or heat level of a meal.
is-this-dish-spicy.exampleSentence: I have a delicate stomach; is this dish spicy?

water-without-ice-please.exampleSentence: Just a glass of tap or bottled water without ice, please.

delicious-compliment.text: The food was delicious, thank you
delicious-compliment.meaningNote: Hearty praise for the cook and dining staff.
delicious-compliment.exampleSentence: Compliments to the chef, the food was delicious!

is-this-vegetarian.meaningNote: Verifying lack of meat, poultry, or seafood broth.
is-this-vegetarian.exampleSentence: Does this soup contain meat broth, or is it strictly vegetarian?

can-i-have-this-to-go.text: Can I have this to go, please?
can-i-have-this-to-go.meaningNote: Requesting a takeout box for remaining food.
can-i-have-this-to-go.exampleSentence: We could not finish our meal; can I have this to go, please?

what-is-your-name.meaningNote: Polite question when introducing yourself to someone new.
what-is-your-name.exampleSentence: Hello, my name is Alex; what is your name?

it-is-my-first-time-here.text: It is my first time visiting here.
it-is-my-first-time-here.meaningNote: Friendly icebreaker when chatting with locals.
it-is-my-first-time-here.exampleSentence: It is my first time visiting here, and the city is beautiful.

where-are-you-from.meaningNote: Common small-talk question about someone's hometown or country.
where-are-you-from.exampleSentence: We are visiting from Canada; where are you from?

is-this-your-hometown.meaningNote: Asking whether someone grew up in the current city or town.
is-this-your-hometown.exampleSentence: You know the neighborhood so well; is this your hometown?

what-do-you-do-for-a-living.text: What do you do for a living?
what-do-you-do-for-a-living.meaningNote: Polite question about someone's profession or occupation.
what-do-you-do-for-a-living.exampleSentence: I work as a teacher; what do you do for a living?

how-long-have-you-lived-here.text: How long have you lived here?
how-long-have-you-lived-here.meaningNote: Asking a resident how long they have lived in the area.
how-long-have-you-lived-here.exampleSentence: It is a wonderful neighborhood; how long have you lived here?

what-do-you-like-to-do.text: What do you like to do in your free time?
what-do-you-like-to-do.meaningNote: Asking about hobbies and personal interests.
what-do-you-like-to-do.exampleSentence: I enjoy hiking; what do you like to do in your free time?

that-is-interesting.meaningNote: Warm conversational response showing active interest.
that-is-interesting.exampleSentence: That's interesting! I did not know that about the city.

it-was-nice-talking-to-you.text: It was nice talking to you.
it-was-nice-talking-to-you.meaningNote: Polite way to wrap up a conversation before leaving.
it-was-nice-talking-to-you.exampleSentence: I have to catch my train now, but it was nice talking to you.

have-a-nice-day.exampleSentence: Thank you for your time, have a nice day!

how-much-is-this.meaningNote: Essential question when checking the price of an item.
how-much-is-this.exampleSentence: Excuse me, how much is this handmade bag?

is-this-available-in-another-size.text: Is this available in another size?
is-this-available-in-another-size.meaningNote: Asking a clerk for a larger or smaller clothing or shoe size.
is-this-available-in-another-size.exampleSentence: This shirt is a bit small; is this available in another size?

do-you-have-another-color.meaningNote: Checking whether an item comes in other colors.
do-you-have-another-color.exampleSentence: I like this style; do you have another color?

can-i-try-this-on.meaningNote: Asking permission to use the fitting room for clothing or shoes.
can-i-try-this-on.exampleSentence: Excuse me, can I try this on? Where is the fitting room?

is-there-a-discount.meaningNote: Inquiring about current promotions or cash discounts.
is-there-a-discount.exampleSentence: Is there a discount if I pay in cash?

can-you-lower-the-price.meaningNote: Used for friendly bargaining at open-air markets and souvenir stalls.
can-you-lower-the-price.exampleSentence: I would like to buy two; can you lower the price a little?

i-am-just-looking-thank-you.text: I am just looking, thank you.
i-am-just-looking-thank-you.meaningNote: Polite response to a salesperson when browsing without needing help yet.
i-am-just-looking-thank-you.exampleSentence: I am just looking right now, thank you.

where-can-i-find-this-item.text: Where can I find this item?
where-can-i-find-this-item.meaningNote: Asking store staff which aisle or section carries a product.
where-can-i-find-this-item.exampleSentence: Excuse me, where can I find this item in the store?

can-i-return-this.meaningNote: Asking about the store's return or exchange policy.
can-i-return-this.exampleSentence: If it does not fit, can I return this tomorrow with the receipt?

can-i-get-a-shopping-bag.text: Can I get a shopping bag?
can-i-get-a-shopping-bag.meaningNote: Requesting a carrier bag at checkout.
can-i-get-a-shopping-bag.exampleSentence: Can I get a shopping bag for these groceries, please?

what-time-is-it.meaningNote: Asking for the current time of day.
what-time-is-it.exampleSentence: Excuse me, what time is it right now?

what-day-is-today.meaningNote: Asking for the day of the week.
what-day-is-today.exampleSentence: What day is today? Is the museum open on Mondays?

what-is-todays-date.meaningNote: Asking for the calendar date (month and day).
what-is-todays-date.exampleSentence: I need to fill out this form; what is today's date?

when-does-it-open.meaningNote: Asking for the opening hour of a business, museum, or office.
when-does-it-open.exampleSentence: The door is still locked; when does it open?

when-does-it-close.meaningNote: Checking closing hours so you can plan your visit.
when-does-it-close.exampleSentence: We want to visit this evening; when does it close?

how-long-will-it-take.meaningNote: Asking for the estimated duration of a trip, wait, or service.
how-long-will-it-take.exampleSentence: How long will it take to get there by bus?

can-we-meet-tomorrow.meaningNote: Arranging an appointment or meetup for the next day.
can-we-meet-tomorrow.exampleSentence: I am busy this afternoon; can we meet tomorrow instead?

what-time-should-i-come-back.text: What time should I come back?
what-time-should-i-come-back.meaningNote: Useful when dropping off laundry, waiting for a table, or returning for a tour.
what-time-should-i-come-back.exampleSentence: I will leave my bags now; what time should I come back?

two-tickets-please.meaningNote: Useful number phrase for buying admission or transit tickets.
two-tickets-please.exampleSentence: Good morning, two tickets for the ten o'clock tour, please.

for-how-many-people.meaningNote: Common quantity question heard or asked at restaurants, tours, and hotels.
for-how-many-people.exampleSentence: We need a reservation for tonight—for how many people?

do-you-speak-english.meaningNote: Polite question before switching to English with a stranger.
do-you-speak-english.exampleSentence: Excuse me, do you speak English?

i-do-not-understand.meaningNote: Letting the speaker know you did not catch their meaning.
i-do-not-understand.exampleSentence: I am sorry, I don't understand what that means.

could-you-speak-more-slowly.meaningNote: Asking someone to slow down so you can follow along.
could-you-speak-more-slowly.exampleSentence: Could you speak more slowly, please? I am still learning.

could-you-repeat-that.meaningNote: Asking someone to say the last sentence again.
could-you-repeat-that.exampleSentence: I missed the last part; could you repeat that, please?

could-you-write-it-down.meaningNote: Helpful for addresses, prices, or unfamiliar place names.
could-you-write-it-down.exampleSentence: Could you write it down on this paper so I don't forget?

how-do-you-say-this.text: How do you say this in your language?
how-do-you-say-this.meaningNote: Useful when pointing to an object or word to learn its local name.
how-do-you-say-this.exampleSentence: How do you say this in your language?

what-does-this-mean.meaningNote: Asking for the meaning of an unfamiliar word on a sign or menu.
what-does-this-mean.exampleSentence: Excuse me, what does this word mean on the sign?

i-am-learning-your-language.meaningNote: Encourages patience and warm conversation from locals.
i-am-learning-your-language.exampleSentence: Please forgive my mistakes; I am learning your language.

please-wait-a-moment.meaningNote: Polite way to ask someone to pause while you check your bag or phone.
please-wait-a-moment.exampleSentence: Please wait a moment while I look up the address.

can-you-show-me.meaningNote: Asking someone to demonstrate or point something out directly.
can-you-show-me.exampleSentence: I am not sure how this ticket machine works; can you show me?

this-is-my-family.meaningNote: Introducing family members or showing a family photo.
this-is-my-family.exampleSentence: Hello, this is my family visiting with me.

i-am-traveling-with-my-parents.text: I am traveling with my parents.
i-am-traveling-with-my-parents.meaningNote: Explaining that you are on a trip with your mother and father.
i-am-traveling-with-my-parents.exampleSentence: I am traveling with my parents on their first trip abroad.

do-you-have-children.exampleSentence: We have two kids; do you have children?

where-is-your-family.meaningNote: Asking where someone's family is located or lives.
where-is-your-family.exampleSentence: Do they live nearby, or where is your family?

i-am-here-with-a-friend.text: I am here with a friend.
i-am-here-with-a-friend.meaningNote: Mentioning that you are visiting with a companion.
i-am-here-with-a-friend.exampleSentence: I am here with a friend from college.

this-is-my-friend.meaningNote: Used to introduce a friend to someone.
this-is-my-friend.exampleSentence: Hello, this is my friend Elena.

this-is-my-partner.meaningNote: Introducing your romantic partner or spouse.
this-is-my-partner.exampleSentence: Nice to meet you; this is my partner, Sam.

i-have-a-brother-and-a-sister.text: I have a brother and a sister.
i-have-a-brother-and-a-sister.meaningNote: Sharing how many siblings you have.
i-have-a-brother-and-a-sister.exampleSentence: I come from a small family; I have a brother and a sister.

do-you-have-brothers-or-sisters.text: Do you have brothers or sisters?
do-you-have-brothers-or-sisters.meaningNote: Asking someone if they have siblings.
do-you-have-brothers-or-sisters.exampleSentence: Do you have brothers or sisters, or are you an only child?

how-old-are-your-children.meaningNote: Friendly follow-up question when someone mentions their children.
how-old-are-your-children.exampleSentence: How old are your children now?

where-is-the-bathroom.exampleSentence: Excuse me, where is the bathroom located in this building?

how-do-i-get-to-the-station.text: How do I get to the train station?
how-do-i-get-to-the-station.meaningNote: Asking route guidance towards railway transit.
how-do-i-get-to-the-station.exampleSentence: Pardon me, how do I get to the central train station from here?

is-it-far-from-here.meaningNote: Estimating walking feasibility versus vehicle hire.
is-it-far-from-here.exampleSentence: Can we walk there, or is it far from here?

turn-left-at-the-corner.text: Turn left at the next corner
turn-left-at-the-corner.meaningNote: Navigation command directing a left turn.
turn-left-at-the-corner.exampleSentence: Walk two blocks, then turn left at the next corner.

turn-right-after-the-bank.exampleSentence: Keep going straight and turn right after the bank.

go-straight-ahead.meaningNote: Instruction to maintain the current heading without turning.
go-straight-ahead.exampleSentence: Go straight ahead until you see the cathedral.

where-am-i-on-the-map.text: Where am I on this map?
where-am-i-on-the-map.meaningNote: Asking a passerby to pinpoint your current location.
where-am-i-on-the-map.exampleSentence: I lost my orientation; where am I on this map?

is-it-within-walking-distance.meaningNote: Inquiring if a destination can be reached comfortably by foot.
is-it-within-walking-distance.exampleSentence: Is the museum within walking distance from our hotel?

where-is-the-bus-stop.text: Where is the nearest bus stop?
where-is-the-bus-stop.exampleSentence: Could you tell me where the nearest bus stop is?

i-am-lost-can-you-help.text: I am lost, can you help me?
i-am-lost-can-you-help.meaningNote: Courteous plea for navigational help when disoriented.
i-am-lost-can-you-help.exampleSentence: Excuse me, I am lost, can you help me find my hotel?

where-is-baggage-claim.text: Where is the baggage claim area?
where-is-baggage-claim.meaningNote: Inquiring about carousel location upon flight landing.
where-is-baggage-claim.exampleSentence: Our flight just landed; where is the baggage claim area?

i-have-a-hotel-reservation.text: I have a reservation under this name
i-have-a-hotel-reservation.meaningNote: Standard introduction at hotel front desk check-in.
i-have-a-hotel-reservation.exampleSentence: Good afternoon, I have a reservation under Sarah Jenkins.

what-time-is-checkout.exampleSentence: Could you tell me what time checkout is tomorrow morning?

how-much-is-a-ticket-to.text: How much is a ticket to the city center?
how-much-is-a-ticket-to.exampleSentence: Hello, how much is a one-way ticket to the city center?

which-platform-for-the-airport.text: Which platform does the airport train leave from?
which-platform-for-the-airport.meaningNote: Track or platform navigation in a rail station.
which-platform-for-the-airport.exampleSentence: Excuse me, which platform does the airport express leave from?

can-you-call-a-taxi.text: Could you call a taxi for me, please?
can-you-call-a-taxi.meaningNote: Requesting transport assistance from hotel staff or a business.
can-you-call-a-taxi.exampleSentence: I have heavy bags; could you call a taxi for me, please?

do-you-have-wifi.text: Do you have Wi-Fi here, and what is the password?
do-you-have-wifi.exampleSentence: Excuse me, do you have Wi-Fi here, and what is the password?

can-i-leave-my-luggage-here.text: Can I leave my luggage here for a few hours?
can-i-leave-my-luggage-here.meaningNote: Temporary baggage storage request before room readiness or after checkout.
can-i-leave-my-luggage-here.exampleSentence: Our flight departs late; can I leave my luggage here for a few hours?

do-you-accept-credit-cards.text: Do you accept credit cards or cash only?
do-you-accept-credit-cards.meaningNote: Clarifying payment methods before ordering goods or services.
do-you-accept-credit-cards.exampleSentence: Before we order, do you accept credit cards or cash only?

where-can-i-exchange-currency.text: Where can I safely exchange currency?
where-can-i-exchange-currency.meaningNote: Locating an authorized foreign currency exchange office.
where-can-i-exchange-currency.exampleSentence: Excuse me, where can I safely exchange foreign currency nearby?

help-me-please.text: Please help me! / I need help
help-me-please.meaningNote: Urgent, universal cry for immediate assistance in distress.
help-me-please.exampleSentence: Please help me, somebody grabbed my backpack!

call-an-ambulance.meaningNote: Direct medical emergency instruction to bystanders.
call-an-ambulance.exampleSentence: Someone collapsed; please call an ambulance immediately!

call-the-police.meaningNote: Instruction to contact law enforcement immediately.
call-the-police.exampleSentence: There has been a break-in; please call the police right now!

where-is-the-nearest-hospital.text: Where is the nearest hospital or clinic?
where-is-the-nearest-hospital.exampleSentence: My companion has severe abdominal pain; where is the nearest hospital?

i-need-a-doctor.text: I need to see a doctor who speaks English
i-need-a-doctor.meaningNote: Requesting a bilingual physician to guarantee clear clinical diagnosis.
i-need-a-doctor.exampleSentence: I feel unwell and need to see a doctor who speaks English.

where-is-a-pharmacy.text: Where is the nearest open pharmacy?
where-is-a-pharmacy.exampleSentence: I have a headache; where is the nearest open pharmacy?

i-lost-my-passport.text: I lost my passport and wallet
i-lost-my-passport.meaningNote: Reporting missing legal identification and funds to authorities.
i-lost-my-passport.exampleSentence: I need help reaching my embassy because I lost my passport.

i-cannot-breathe.meaningNote: Critical indicator of asthma, allergic anaphylaxis, or cardiac issues.
i-cannot-breathe.exampleSentence: Please sit me up and assist me, I am having trouble breathing.

there-is-a-fire.text: There is a fire, evacuate the building!
there-is-a-fire.meaningNote: Urgent hazard warning to prompt building evacuation.
there-is-a-fire.exampleSentence: I smell thick smoke; there is a fire, evacuate the building!

i-feel-very-dizzy.text: I feel very dizzy and weak
i-feel-very-dizzy.exampleSentence: I need to sit down immediately; I feel very dizzy and weak.
